user.title: Which rooms should Calm look after?
user.description: Calm needs at least one lamp and a light sensor. You can still tick a room without a light sensor; you pick one in the next step.

sensor.title: {room} has no light sensor yet
sensor.description: Pick a light sensor from another room. One in the room next door works well, and an outdoor sensor at least knows when it gets dark. Leave it empty and Calm skips this room for now.

when.title: When may Calm run the lamps?
when.description: This applies to every room; you can change it per room later. Everything you switch on here has to hold.

data_description.home: Follows the people in Home Assistant.

condition.name: When something is on or off
condition.description: For example: only while night mode is off.

data.entity_state: Calm may run when it is

data_description.entity: Leave empty if you do not use this.

data.manual: I run it myself with an automation

data_description.manual: Calm then only does what the room's Calm switch says, and looks at none of the conditions above.

rhythm.title: Your day
rhythm.description: In the morning the light rises from warm to bright, and in the evening it grows warmer and softer towards bedtime.

abort.no_rooms: No lamps are in a room in Home Assistant yet. Put your lamps in areas first (Settings → Areas), and Calm finds them by itself.
abort.single_instance_allowed: Calm is already installed. Add rooms under Calm.

rooms.title: Which rooms should Calm look after?
rooms.description: Untick a room and Calm stops there, and forgets that room's settings and overrides.

room_sensor.title: {room} has no light sensor yet
room_sensor.description: Pick a light sensor from another room. Leave it empty and this room is not added.

data_description.threshold_lux: When the daylight is below this, the lamps come on. It is the same all day. {reading}
data_description.brightness: The highest level during the day.
data_description.evening_brightness: Where the light sinks to, unseen, in the last hour and a half before bed, after it has turned warm first. Never brighter than by day.

data.use_motion: Only light when somebody is in the room

data_description.motion_always: Even when Calm is off: a nightlight at night, ordinary light during the day.

data_description.own_when: Off: this room follows Calm → Configure → When. On: you set it on the next screen.

data_description.own_rhythm: Off: this room follows Calm → Configure → Rhythm. On: you set it on the next screen.

data_description.excluded_lights: A worktop light that only belongs to a work light, for example.
data_description.light_sensor: Empty: the sensor Calm found in the room.
data_description.min_level: Below this the lamps do nothing; the room goes off rather than dimming further.
data_description.manual_hold_minutes: How long Calm leaves the lamps alone after somebody sets them by hand.

data.override: Pick one to change, or make a new one

override_new.title: New override
override_new.description: Pick a template. Then choose which lamps take part and adjust the rest. The name becomes the switch's name and cannot change later.

data_description.level: Relative to normal: 100% is the same, 200% twice as much. As a set level: the lamp's percentage.
data_description.auto_state: Usually 'on'. For a TV, 'playing' may fit better.
data_description.remove: The switch goes too, and an automation pointing at it stops working.

condition_missing.title: Calm is watching something that no longer exists
condition_missing.description:
Calm only runs the lamps when {entity} is in the chosen state, but that entity no longer exists, so the lamps stay off.

Choose another under Settings → Devices & services → Calm → Configure → When, or in the room itself if it has its own ‘when’.
